DboY_thD7dM.attention: The black card rising above white peaks against a blue sky, with a red climber planting a flag.
takeaways: Post the finished campaign image first, then the props behind it.
Include one frame showing the real size of a prop that looks huge on camera.
End a making-of carousel on the work in its public placement.
Keep the offer and its terms together in the caption when the images carry no offer copy.
DboY_thD7dM.adaptation: A bakery launching a wedding-cake line could open on the styled cake shot, then show piping tools, the lighting setup and the shop-window display.
DboY_thD7dM.use: The campaign’s craft is part of its appeal and the making-of material is visually interesting.
DboY_thD7dM.avoid: The audience needs the offer details first, since these frames carry almost no product information.

Dbd7FT2FGd3.intent: Show the savings contest’s out-of-home campaign in place and point viewers to its details.
Dbd7FT2FGd3.brand: Each poster ends with the serif Wealthsimple wordmark beside “Monthly Millionaire” on a deep blue ground.
Dbd7FT2FGd3.composition: Photos frame the posters off-centre or straight-on within tiled walls and platforms, often with people passing in front.
Dbd7FT2FGd3.typography: A small sentence-case tip tops each poster, a huge lowercase two-line promise crosses the subject, and a short entry line sits above the wordmark.
Dbd7FT2FGd3.colour: Saturated blue posters stand out against beige tiles, a dark platform and a yellow safety strip.
Dbd7FT2FGd3.imagery: Studio portraits inside the posters show people overloaded with cabbages, furniture, dresses or a freshly cut fringe.
Dbd7FT2FGd3.devices: Motion-blurred commuters and a station sign place each poster in a real transit setting.
Dbd7FT2FGd3.arc: A two-poster platform view opens, three single-poster placements follow, and the cabbage poster closes the set in a wider frame.
Dbd7FT2FGd3.copy: The poster headline repeats one promise, each tip line changes the saving habit, and the caption jokes about signs while flagging terms.
Dbd7FT2FGd3.attention: The oversized cream “become a millionaire” lettering stands out against the blue posters.
takeaways: Keep one large promise fixed and rotate a small tip line across the series.
Choose props that make each tip visible without reading.
Shoot outdoor placements with passers-by or signage to show where the ads live.
Repeat the contest terms on every frame of the carousel.
Dbd7FT2FGd3.adaptation: A library card campaign could pair small habits such as “Borrow, don’t buy” with a giant “build a bookshelf” line, photographed in stations.
Dbd7FT2FGd3.use: A contest or reward builds up from everyday behaviour and the ads run in visible public places.
Dbd7FT2FGd3.avoid: The prize odds are so long that a literal promise could read as a guarantee.

DbbgY7DD4Ay.topic: Pilot Coffee pop-up in an airport lounge
DbbgY7DD4Ay.intent: Announce a coffee partnership and its card cash-back perk through the objects and signage at the location.
DbbgY7DD4Ay.brand: Wealthsimple’s serif wordmark appears on the cup, the sign and the rack, beside Pilot Coffee’s yellow mark.
DbbgY7DD4Ay.composition: Close crops place single objects in the centre against heavily blurred backgrounds.
DbbgY7DD4Ay.typography: Sans-serif capitals and lowercase sit small on the objects, with the serif wordmark as the brand signature.
DbbgY7DD4Ay.colour: White cups and a black rack stand against soft pastel and warm wood backgrounds.
DbbgY7DD4Ay.imagery: Shallow-focus photographs treat cups, a sign and a rack as product shots.
DbbgY7DD4Ay.devices: Wordplay on the second cup and the rack’s label act as the post’s only headlines.
DbbgY7DD4Ay.arc: The set moves from the co-branded cup to the offer sign, a pun cup and the reading rack nearby.
DbbgY7DD4Ay.copy: The sign’s headline sells the free coffee, the cup pun links coffee to money, and the caption sets the scene at an early airport lounge visit.
DbbgY7DD4Ay.attention: The co-branded cup sits sharp in the centre against a blurred wash of colour.
takeaways: Lead with the shared object that carries both brand names.
Use shallow focus so one printed object reads as the headline.
Write a two-word pun that links the product to your category.
Photograph the offer sign where people will actually redeem it.
DbbgY7DD4Ay.adaptation: A bookstore and a bank could co-brand bookmarks, print “Compound Interest” on one and photograph the till-side offer card.
DbbgY7DD4Ay.use: A partnership has physical touchpoints such as cups, bags or signage at a real location.
DbbgY7DD4Ay.avoid: The offer’s conditions need more explanation than a photographed sign can carry legibly.

DbVsTOHDtqt.intent: Link the card’s cash back on camping essentials to a handmade miniature camping scene and its making.
DbVsTOHDtqt.brand: The card’s embossed W and Visa marks are the only branding, on a matte black card.
DbVsTOHDtqt.composition: The card stands centred as a backdrop while the miniature camp fills the foreground.
DbVsTOHDtqt.typography: No type is added; the only words are the Visa marks printed on the card.
DbVsTOHDtqt.colour: Autumn reds and yellows, grass greens and lake blue surround the dark card.
DbVsTOHDtqt.imagery: Polished diorama photography alternates with casual phone-style shots and video covers from the set.
DbVsTOHDtqt.devices: Giant hands and a camera rig break the miniature illusion on purpose.
DbVsTOHDtqt.arc: A finished hero shot is followed by hands at work, production frames and a close-up of one figurine.
DbVsTOHDtqt.copy: There is no added on-image copy; the caption lists s’mores ingredients before stating the camping cash-back offer and terms.
DbVsTOHDtqt.attention: The flat black card dominates the colourful miniature landscape around it.
takeaways: Build a miniature world where the product is the biggest object.
Add a frame with a real hand to reveal the scale.
Close on one figurine detail that rewards a closer look.
Show the camera rig when the handmade craft is part of the story.
DbVsTOHDtqt.adaptation: A hiking app could stand a phone in a tabletop mountain range, then show hands placing tiny hikers along its trail.
DbVsTOHDtqt.use: The product is a flat object that can act as a backdrop and the offer suggests a scene.
DbVsTOHDtqt.avoid: The offer needs explaining on the image, since the diorama carries no words.

DbTZLyFjrsx.intent: Tease a magazine story in which Canadians share what their jobs pay, and send readers to the full piece.
DbTZLyFjrsx.brand: The serif Wealthsimple wordmark and a “Magazine” label top the cover; the salary slides carry no logo.
DbTZLyFjrsx.composition: Every salary slide stacks a job title, city, huge figure and two quote paragraphs down the left side.
DbTZLyFjrsx.typography: One geometric sans-serif runs in three sizes, from the oversized salary figure to the quote text.
DbTZLyFjrsx.colour: A multicolour cover gives way to dark grounds, each paired with one light accent for title and figure.
DbTZLyFjrsx.imagery: The cover’s paper-textured speech bubbles hold dollar signs; the other slides are type only.
DbTZLyFjrsx.devices: Speech-bubble shapes on the cover signal confession before any figure appears.
DbTZLyFjrsx.arc: A collage cover sets up the series, then five professions follow in one repeated template.
DbTZLyFjrsx.copy: The cover title and subtitle frame the series, each slide’s quote supplies a personal story, and the caption opens with a question about pay.
DbTZLyFjrsx.attention: The white “Salary Confessions” title sits across a crowd of coloured dollar-sign speech bubbles.
takeaways: Set the number people wonder about larger than the job title.
Hold one template steady and switch the background colour per entry.
Keep each quote to two short paragraphs in the speaker’s own words.
Show any add-ons, such as equity or extra fees, directly under the main figure.
DbTZLyFjrsx.adaptation: A rental app could run “Rent Confessions”, one city per slide with the monthly rent huge and a tenant quote beneath.
DbTZLyFjrsx.use: Readers are curious about figures people rarely share, and contributors can stay anonymous.
DbTZLyFjrsx.avoid: The figures need a common basis, such as annual pre-tax pay, that the slides cannot show.

DbEYAZyjzZb.topic: Credit card sculpture at an airport pop-up
DbEYAZyjzZb.intent: Invite people to look closely at a pop-up sculpture whose props spell out the card’s travel features.
DbEYAZyjzZb.brand: Gold-foil Wealthsimple wordmarks and W medallions mark the passport and coins beside the black Visa card.
DbEYAZyjzZb.composition: Wide frames centre the round silver plinth; close-ups crop tight on a single prop with blurred surroundings.
DbEYAZyjzZb.typography: Monospace receipt type, engraved coin-edge capitals and a serif wordmark each match the object they sit on.
DbEYAZyjzZb.colour: A gradient of yellow, coral and purple cards glows against the black passport, metal coins and pale lounge walls.
DbEYAZyjzZb.imagery: Warmly lit product photography treats the props as sculpture, with shallow focus on each detail.
DbEYAZyjzZb.devices: Repeated text bands on the coin edge and the stamp ring turn single phrases into patterns.
DbEYAZyjzZb.arc: The whole sculpture opens, seven close-ups find a feature in each prop, and a frontal view of the whole closes.
DbEYAZyjzZb.copy: Every word sits on a prop: the receipt title names cash back, the coin and stamps repeat fee lines, and the caption invites a close look.
DbEYAZyjzZb.attention: The fan of translucent gradient cards catches the light at the centre of the plinth.
takeaways: Assign each product benefit to one prop that can carry its words.
Repeat a phrase around an edge or stamp so it still reads in a tight crop.
Open and close the carousel on the full display so the close-ups have context.
Write a mock receipt in the brand’s voice to list benefits as line items.
DbEYAZyjzZb.adaptation: A meal-kit brand could build a giant lunchbox whose labels, receipt and utensils each spell out one plan feature.
DbEYAZyjzZb.use: A product has several short, concrete features and a physical space where people can explore.
DbEYAZyjzZb.avoid: Features depend on conditions or rates that props can only hint at.

DbDxlRhjouk.intent: Explain how a futures trade works in plain steps and close with reasons to trade futures on Wealthsimple.
DbDxlRhjouk.brand: Wealthsimple appears only as the last card’s heading and in the regulatory footer; no logo is shown.
DbDxlRhjouk.composition: A large rounded frosted card sits centred on every slide, inset from a soft gradient border.
DbDxlRhjouk.typography: A bold geometric sans heading sits above lighter centred body text, with a small circled numeral on top.
DbDxlRhjouk.colour: Gradient borders move from pink and orange through olive to green and blue across the carousel.
DbDxlRhjouk.imagery: There are no photographs; blurred concentric squares of colour form the only imagery.
DbDxlRhjouk.devices: Circled numerals and a constant frosted card frame each step.
DbDxlRhjouk.arc: A question cover is followed by an analogy, three trade steps and a pitch card.
DbDxlRhjouk.copy: Headings state each step in a short sentence, body text explains it, and the caption jokes that futures have nothing to do with tarot.
DbDxlRhjouk.attention: The white two-line question stands out against the soft concentric colour squares.
takeaways: Start a technical topic with an everyday analogy on the first card.
Number each card so readers can see how long the explanation runs.
Keep the card layout fixed and let the border colour change per step.
Label a closing sales card honestly instead of disguising it as a step.
DbDxlRhjouk.adaptation: A mortgage broker could explain a variable rate in four numbered cards, opening with an analogy, and flag a fifth card as the pitch.
DbDxlRhjouk.use: A financial product needs a short, ordered explanation before any pitch.
DbDxlRhjouk.avoid: The product’s risks need more room than a four-step card format allows.

Da24cKkDvOr.topic: Portfolio line of credit for debt
Da24cKkDvOr.intent: Persuade people carrying credit-card debt to move it to a portfolio line of credit secured by their investments.
Da24cKkDvOr.brand: Wealthsimple is named only in the footnotes; the slides rely on a beige gradient and geometric sans.
Da24cKkDvOr.composition: Headlines anchor the top left and explanations the bottom left, with empty gradient between them.
Da24cKkDvOr.typography: Large charcoal sans-serif headlines use italic underlined words for emphasis over lighter body text.
Da24cKkDvOr.colour: A warm beige-to-tan gradient runs behind charcoal type on every slide.
Da24cKkDvOr.imagery: One 3D staircase render appears on the cover; the remaining slides are type only.
Da24cKkDvOr.devices: Thick underlines under italic words mark each reframe.
Da24cKkDvOr.arc: A debt question opens, a one-word twist reframes it, two slides explain the product and a win-win closes.
Da24cKkDvOr.copy: Headlines carry the argument in questions and short claims, body copy adds rates and mechanics, and the caption warns against cashing out investments.
Da24cKkDvOr.attention: The large two-line question sits above an isolated 3D staircase.
takeaways: Insert one word into the audience’s problem to point toward your product.
Mark the reframing word with one emphasis style used nowhere else.
Place the claim at the top and the explanation at the bottom of a quiet background.
State the rate’s range and date next to any “as low as” figure.
Da24cKkDvOr.adaptation: A meal-prep service could ask “Do you have a cooking problem?” and then reframe it as a planning problem, underlining “planning”.
Da24cKkDvOr.use: The audience’s problem can be reframed so the product becomes the obvious fix.
Da24cKkDvOr.avoid: The reframe would gloss over real risks, such as borrowing against investments that can fall.

Davt6OPD8wG.topic: TLDR print edition at an airport lounge
Davt6OPD8wG.intent: Show off a special print issue of the TLDR newsletter, from its production to readers in an airport lounge.
Davt6OPD8wG.brand: The bold TLDR wordmark with a money-face emoji sits under a small serif Wealthsimple on every copy.
Davt6OPD8wG.composition: Most frames crop close on hands, racks or pages, with deep blur keeping attention on the newspaper.
Davt6OPD8wG.typography: A heavy black TLDR wordmark and condensed cover headlines contrast with the serif Wealthsimple logo.
Davt6OPD8wG.colour: Off-white newsprint stands out against black racks, warm amber light and the emoji’s yellow.
Davt6OPD8wG.imagery: Candid-style photographs of people with the paper mix with two video covers and a phone screen.
Davt6OPD8wG.devices: A repeated money-face emoji and QR code tie every masthead together.
Davt6OPD8wG.arc: The set moves from picking up a copy to racks, production, reading, the sign-up page and the lounge entrance.
Davt6OPD8wG.copy: The cover headline promises investing advice, the masthead claims readership, and the caption jokes about putting backs into the print run.
Davt6OPD8wG.attention: A hand lifting a copy shows the TLDR masthead at an angle against dark shadow.
takeaways: Photograph printed pieces mid-use: lifted, read, carried.
Fill one frame with repeated mastheads to fix the name.
Show the digital sign-up screen next to the physical giveaway.
Close on the venue so viewers know where to find the copies.
Davt6OPD8wG.adaptation: A recipe newsletter could print a market-day edition and show it picked up at stalls, read on benches and linked to a sign-up QR code.
Davt6OPD8wG.use: A brand distributes a physical edition of digital content at a specific place.
Davt6OPD8wG.avoid: The publication is only digital, so there is nothing tangible for people to handle.

DavMssAOOsk.intent: Show that several popular stocks gained mostly outside trading hours, as a teaser for a TLDR newsletter story.
DavMssAOOsk.brand: A heavy TLDR wordmark with the money-face emoji anchors the bottom right corner.
DavMssAOOsk.composition: A left column of stock names lines up with nine horizontal dumbbells over a dotted vertical grid.
DavMssAOOsk.typography: A bold two-line question headline sits over a lighter subhead, with white figures set inside the pills.
DavMssAOOsk.colour: Green daytime and periwinkle overnight pills on a pale mint ground keep the two series apart.
DavMssAOOsk.imagery: A single dumbbell chart is the only image, with no photos or illustrations.
DavMssAOOsk.devices: Rounded pills joined by olive lines form each row’s dumbbell.
DavMssAOOsk.arc: The question and subhead set up the anomaly, the legend explains the colours, the rows give the figures and the footer gives sources.
DavMssAOOsk.copy: The headline poses a spooky question, the subhead frames the anomaly, and the caption names the reporter and the term “overnight drift”.
DavMssAOOsk.attention: Long olive lines run to GameStop’s and Strategy’s blue pills near the right edge.
takeaways: Use a dumbbell row when two measures per item tell the story.
Print each value inside its marker so readers can skip the axis.
Name the start and end dates of the time window under the chart.
Open a data post with a familiar phrase that hints at the pattern.
DavMssAOOsk.adaptation: A transit agency could chart weekday against weekend ridership per line as paired pills, under the headline “Who rides on Sundays?”.
DavMssAOOsk.use: Each item has two comparable measures and the gap between them is the point.
DavMssAOOsk.avoid: There are many series per item, or the values differ so much that the axis squeezes most rows.
